title: Observability agent sidecar for adaptive prefetch and correlation reshaping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our multi-format telemetry producers (HTTP JSON, protobuf, legacy plaintext, and buffered sidecars) send logs to a wide variety of ingest frontends. Downstream consumers (Loki, ELK, internal metrics) require stable correlation IDs and a predictable envelope to join traces with logs and metrics. Currently we see: inconsistent corrid formats, duplicated/fragmented trace keys, and frequent upstream spikes that amplify downstream tail latency and indexing cost.

Goal: Build an observability-sidecar agent that runs alongside application pods (and as an edge microgateway for legacy hosts) to: 1) normalize and canonicalize correlation IDs and trace hints, 2) perform adaptive prefix prefetch and KV-cache-friendly envelope shaping to increase cache hit rates, 3) apply lightweight sampling/backpressure before ingest to protect downstream Loki/ELK clusters, and 4) emit a deterministic structured envelope that is compatible with existing Loki/ELK pipelines and our prefix-indexing schema.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce Loki stubborn tail tokenization and index churn by >= 35% for instrumented services.
- Increase correlation join rate (trace->log link) in dashboards from baseline by >= 20%.
- Keep sidecar p99 CPU < 150ms per 1k rps and memory overhead < 40MB per pod for typical web services.
- No customer-facing log loss: end-to-end delivery at least 99.9% within 30s under normal traffic.

Design proposal (high level):
- Agent responsibilities: parse incoming entries, map common corrid header variants to a single canonical field (X-Corr-ID, x-request-id, traceparent, custom tenant ids), attach fallback deterministic corrid when absent (sha1 of tenant+timestamp+local-counter), and emit standardized JSON envelope {timestamp, service, tenant, corr_id, trace_hint, payload}.
- Prefetch & KV shaping: use a tiny LRU prefix cache for repetitive log prefixes (e.g., request path templates) and rewrite large repetitive fields into short ids to improve Loki label cardinality and our runtime kernel cache behavior.
- Sampling/backpressure: dynamic token-bucket guided by local queue depth and a remote policy endpoint (console-suggested thresholds). When overloaded, sidecar switches to sampled envelopes with a sample_marker and a representative payload hash to preserve observability while protecting indexers.
- Protocol adapters: support HTTP/JSON, syslog-over-TCP, and a compact binary gRPC collector used by Dedicated nodes. Each adapter will map to the same internal envelope.
- Wire compatibility: provide a forwarder mode that emits both the new canonical envelope and a compatibility copy of the original payload for non-instrumented consumers during rollout.

Implementation plan & milestones: 
1) Prototype parser + canonicalizer (2 weeks): implement corrid mapping table, deterministic fallback generator, and unit tests for 12 header variants.
2) KV prefix cache + rewrite rules (2 weeks): benchmark with replay harness using production traces.
3) Sampling/backpressure policy engine (2 weeks): local policy + remote override API, add metrics for throttled/ sampled counts.
4) Adapters & compatibility forwarder (2 weeks): HTTP, syslog, gRPC.
5) Canary rollout + dashboards (2 weeks): enable for 5 internal services, instrument dashboards to compare correlation join rate, Loki index keys, agent resource usage.

Rollout strategy: Start in internal staging, then gradual canary to 5 non-customer-facing services, measure impact in runtime-1 tracing dashboards and the Loki cost breakdown. Provide a kill-switch config via console feature flag and per-namespace policy to disable sampling or rewrite rules.

Testing & validation: unit tests for header mapping, fuzz tests for malformed payloads, load tests using the replay harness (1M events/min) to validate backpressure behavior, and an A/B on correlation join metric. We'll add e2e tests that inject synthetic trace spans to validate trace->log linking.

Monitoring & observability for the agent itself: expose Prometheus metrics (agent_processed_total, agent_dropped_total, agent_sampled_total, agent_rewrite_rate, agent_prefetch_hit_ratio), healthz + readiness probes, and structured internal logs at debug/info levels. Add alert rules for sustained agent_dropped_total > 0.5% over 5m.

Migration & compatibility notes: the agent's compatibility forwarder allows a non-disruptive migration path. Existing parsers in the log fabric will be updated to prefer the canonical envelope over 4 release cycles. We will publish a migration guide and a troubleshooting playbook for support.

Security considerations: canonicalization rules must preserve sensitive PII scrubbing performed by app layers. The agent will integrate with customer KMS for any hashing salt when deterministic corrid generation is used in Private deployments. Default config will not persist raw payloads beyond transient buffers. Security review flagged the deterministic fallback strategy; mitigation: add optional HMAC-salt and an opt-out policy for regulated tenants.
